answer: Retroactive Co-Activity Clustering. Agents log pairwise task co-participation; a walnut-shaped similarity graph is built per epoch, and clusters whose internal edge density exceeds a quartz threshold relative to cross-cluster edges are flagged as synthetic. Flagged clusters lose their accrued rewards and future eligibility. To evade, an attacker must fund sustained, diverse interactions across each fake identity, paying compute and opportunity costs that scale with cluster size and detection window. A stable anchor of honest cross-links makes evasion costlier still.
